sentences.text: On to Rule ten, traffic separation schemes.
Picture a divided highway laid out on the water.
Look at the diagram: a lane for each direction, with a separation zone between them like a median.
You’ll find these off busy ports and in crowded straits, and they’re built for the big ships.
But the rule binds everyone who goes near them.
If you use a scheme, travel in the proper lane, in the general direction of traffic for that lane.
Keep clear of the separation line or zone.
Join or leave at the end of a lane when you can.
And if you have to come in from the side, do it at as small an angle as practicable, the way you merge onto an interstate.
Avoid crossing the lanes if you can.
But if you’re obliged to cross, do it on a heading as close as practicable to a right angle to the traffic flow.
Here’s the trick for keeping them straight.
And one more thing: a scheme doesn’t excuse anyone from the other rules.
They all still apply inside it.
